title: Rectangular block
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero degrees for all axes and a translation vector of [0.3787, 0.0506, 0.0]. Next, draw a two-dimensional sketch on the first face. This sketch consists of a single loop made up of four lines. The first line starts at the origin (0.0, 0.0) and ends at (0.3713, 0.0). The second line starts at (0.3713, 0.0) and ends at (0.3713, 0.1485). The third line starts at (0.3713, 0.1485) and ends at (0.0, 0.1485). Finally, the fourth line completes the loop by starting at (0.0, 0.1485) and ending at the origin (0.0, 0.0). Scale the entire two-dimensional sketch by a factor of 0.3713. Transform this scaled sketch into three dimensions using the previously defined coordinate system. Extrude the transformed sketch 0.0292 units along the normal direction, ensuring no extrusion occurs in the opposite direction. Integrate the extruded shape into a new solid body. The resulting rectangular block has a length of 0.37128907557698493, a width of 0.148515630230794, and a height of 0.02919682276128109.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Define the initial coordinate system transformation
translation_vector = (0.3787, 0.0506, 0.0)
euler_angles = (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)

# Create the sketch
sketch = cq.Workplane("XY").moveTo(0, 0).lineTo(0.3713, 0).lineTo(0.3713, 0.1485).lineTo(0, 0.1485).close()

# Extrude the sketch
extrusion_depth = 0.0292
block = sketch.extrude(extrusion_depth)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
block = block.translate(translation_vector).rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), euler_angles[0]) \
               .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 1, 0), euler_angles[1]) \
               .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), euler_angles[2])

# Final model
r = block

# Extrude the sketch to create the rectangular plate

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
r = r.translate(translation_vector).rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), euler_angles[0]) \
